title: Cancer of unknown primary, sarcoma and skin cancers

steps.tx: **Cancer of unknown primary** presents with metastatic disease and an occult primary site. A complete history with examination is the first step in the workup of these patients. **CT** imaging of chest, abdomen and pelvis localises the likely primary site in many cases. **PET CT** refines localisation before site directed therapy is chosen in these patients.

steps.tx: **Soft tissue sarcoma** presents as deep enlarging masses in extremities in many cases. **MRI** defines compartment involvement before surgical planning in these patients. **Wide excision** with clear margins is the surgical standard for localised sarcoma in many cases. **Radiation** improves local control in large high grade extremity sarcoma in many protocols.

steps.tx: **Merkel cell carcinoma** is an aggressive skin neuroendocrine tumour of sun exposed skin. **Sentinel node** assessment stages clinically negative Merkel disease in many centres. **Radiation** is adjuvant therapy for localised Merkel disease in many protocols globally. **Mohs surgery** spares tissue in facial basal cell carcinoma in many centres today.
